newsitem.title: USA: September U.S. vehicle sales seen flat to up.
newsitem.headline: September U.S. vehicle sales seen flat to up.

text.p: Cars and light trucks in September sold at an even to slightly higher daily rate compared with a year ago, analysts said Monday, with Detroit's Big Three likely to report another month of mixed results.
Analysts expect Chrysler Corp to report a sales increase of at least 10 percent. Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp, which continue to battle slow car sales, are seen posting flat to down totals.

"The biggest story here is the sales climate is really flat," said Paul Ballew, chief economist at J.D. Power and Associates. "It's a pretty stable selling environment and there's nothing really causing deviation."

Analysts generally expect a seasonally adjusted annual selling rate in the mid-14 million range for September, down from 15 million a year ago, and 15.8 million in August of this year. However, analysts cautioned that the factor supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department to compute the rate distorts the actual sales pace and does not account for sales of about 900,000 units in the month.
"It's the biggest distortion we've had so far this year," said Mike Luckey, president of Luckey Consulting Group.

Light trucks -- which include pickup trucks, minivans and sport/utility vehicles -- are again expected to outsell passenger cars on a daily selling rate basis. September had 24 selling days, versus 25 in the year-ago month.

David Healy, an analyst at Burnham Securities Inc, projects light trucks sales will rise a total of nine percent, versus a four percent decline for car sales. He said "Inventory shortages of popular truck models probably held down September's selling rate for the Big Three to a degree."
Passenger car sales at GM, whose factories are changing over to several new car lines, are expected to fall 11 percent, according to Healy.
Strong pickup and sport/utility sales continue to drive Ford's sales. Recent incentive additions to the Taurus won't begin to be seen in sales until October and November, said Ballew.
"They're trying to win the sales race and that's going to affect October and November," he said.
At Chrysler, analysts predict another monthly increase from last year, with gains in both cars and light trucks.

Chrysler is scheduled to report sales October 1. Ford will report on October 3. GM has typically reported on the first business day of the month, but recently has been delaying it until the second business day.
